'''Lajos Peter Balogh''' (born January 15, 1950), mainly referred to as '''Lou Balogh''', is a Hungarian-American scientist known for his research on [[polymer]]s, [[Dendrimer-encapsulated nanoparticles|dendrimer nanocomposites]], and [[nanomedicine]]. Balogh is the editor-in-chief of [[Precision Nanomedicine]] (PRNANO). Based on his career-long citation numbers, he belongs to the [[doi:10.17632/btchxktzyw|World's Top 2% Scientists]].

== Early life and education ==
Balogh was born on January 15, 1950, in Komádi, Hajdú-Bihar County, Hungary. He studied chemistry at the Debreceni Vegyipari Technikum then at the [[University of Debrecen|Kossuth Lajos University]] from 1969 to 1974, earning his Ph.D. in 1983. In 1991, Balogh received an invitation from the [[University of Massachusetts]] Lowell and moved to the United States.

== Career ==
Balogh joined UMass Lowell as a visiting professor in 1991. In 1996, he left for the [[Michigan Molecular Institute]] to research [[Dendrimer|dendrimers]], where he was a senior associate scientist in [[Donald Tomalia]]'s group. From 1998 to 2018, Balogh worked as a professor at the [[University of Michigan Ann Arbor]], Center for Biologic Nanotechnology, the [[University at Buffalo]], and co-directed  Nano-Biotechnology Center at the [[Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center]]. As a visiting professor, he also taught at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]], the [[Seoul National University Hospital|Seoul National University]], and the [[Semmelweis University]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Macdonald |first=Steph |date=2019-05-10 |title=Weekly digest: what's happening in open science? |url=https://www.openpharma.blog/blog/news/weekly-digest-whats-happening-in-open-science-81/ |access-date=2024-08-12 |website=Open Pharma - Innovations in medical publishing |language=en-US}}</ref>

Balogh is one of the co-founders of the American Society for Nanomedicine (2008). He has been a board member of several expert organizations, e.g., the U.S. Technical Advisory Group to [[International Organization for Standardization|ISO]] TC229 on [[Nanotechnology]] (since 2005), the Scientific Committee of the CLINAM Summits<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Löffler |first=Beat |date=2020-02-11 |title=11 Years of CLINAM, the European Foundation for Clinical Nanomedicine |url=https://precisionnanomedicine.com/article/11897 |journal=Precision Nanomedicine |language=en |volume=3 |issue=1 |pages=483–486 |doi=10.33218/001c.11897|doi-access=free }}</ref> (since 2011), and numerous other National and International Steering Committees.

He has also taught abroad as a visiting professor, holding a visiting professorship for senior international scientists at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] in Beijing, an award of the Korean Federation of Science and Technology Societies Brain Pool programme at [[Seoul National University]], and a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] teaching and research scholarship at [[Semmelweis University]].

Between 2008 and 2016, Balogh was editor-in-chief of scientific journal [[Nanomedicine: Nanotechnology, Biology and Medicine|Nanomedicine: Nanotechnology, Biology, and Medicine]], published by Elsevier. In 2017, Balogh initiated Manuscript Clinic, a platform that helped scientists and students publish their research results in nanomedicine and nanotechnology. In 2018, he founded Andover House, Inc.,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andover House Inc. |url=https://andoverhouse.org/}}</ref> a [[Not-for-profit organization|not-for-profit]] online publishing company, and launched [[Precision Nanomedicine|Precision Nanomedicine (PRNANO)]]. He serves as the editor-in-chief of this journal, whish is official journal of the International Society for Nanomedicine and of CLINAM, the European Society for Clinical Nanomedicine, based in Basel, Switzerland.

== Personal life ==
Balogh is married to Éva Kovács Balogh, a Hungarian American linguist. He has three children, Andrea, Péter, and Áki. Peter Balogh was the crew chief of the [[University of Michigan Solar Car Team|University of Michigan Solar car team]]'s MomentUM, which won first place at the [[North American Solar Challenge 2005|North American Solar Challenge]] in 2005 and now works in the maritime industry in Asia.
